report.summary: Chunk 6 of 7: implements specificity arm functions (_int_arg, _git, commit_shas, measure_commit, specificity, _refs_by_function) for comparing real commits against mutation corpus. Docstrings and comments make claims about behaviour; several are uncheckable due to missing code or external dependencies.
risks: _int_arg | low | Silent fallback on malformed limit; value echoed in report but not validated. | Check if caller relies on default silently.
measure_commit | high | Uses git show with caret syntax (sha^:path); may fail on root commit or non-commit object. | Test with initial commit.
specificity | medium | Returns rows with per_file data; data structure may be large. | Assess memory usage for 80 commits.
_refs_by_function | medium | Function body incomplete (truncated at end of chunk); cannot verify claims about per-function granularity. | Complete the function.
commit_shas | low | Relies on git log with --no-merges and paths; may miss commits that only touch non-Python files. | Confirm intended behaviour.
measure_commit | medium | Skips commits with >max_files files silently (via skipped field); may discard important commits. | Verify if this is intended.
specificity | low | Uses _git which returns None on failure; no retry or error logging. | Add error handling.
todos: Test measure_commit with root commit (sha^ may fail).
Review silent fallback in _int_arg for production use.
Consider adding validation for limit parameter in commit_shas.

handoff.purpose: Implement specificity arm functions: _int_arg, _git, commit_shas, measure_commit, specificity, and partial _refs_by_function.

symbols.name: _int_arg
symbols.note: Extracts integer from argv after flag; returns default on failure.

symbols.name: _git
symbols.note: Runs git command with timeout; returns stdout or None on failure.

symbols.name: commit_shas
symbols.note: Returns list of commit SHAs for non-merge commits touching Python files.

symbols.name: measure_commit
symbols.note: Computes layer delta for a single commit; returns dict with added/removed/type_moved.

symbols.name: specificity
symbols.note: Computes specificity statistics over real commits.

symbols.name: _refs_by_function
symbols.note: Incomplete; intended to return per-function reference multisets.

claims.text: ``--limit 40``, or the default. Silent fallback is deliberate: a malformed limit should not lose the run, and the value is echoed in the written report either way.
claims.why: Function attempts int(argv[argv.index(flag)+1]) and returns default on ValueError/IndexError; silent fallback implemented.

claims.text: Non-merge commits touching Python, newest first. Merges are excluded because a merge's diff against its first parent attributes other people's work to it, which would pollute the corpus with changes it did not make.
claims.why: Function uses 'git log --no-merges' and '--' with paths; returns list of SHAs. Exclusion of merges is correct.

claims.text: The same layer delta, for one real commit. Returns per-file and totals.
claims.why: Function computes added/removed/type_moved per file and totals; returns dict with per_file list.

claims.text: A sweeping commit would dominate the distribution for a reason that has nothing to do with defectiveness. Bounded and SAID, never silently cut.
claims.why: If len(files) > max_files, sets skipped reason and returns early; not silently cut.

claims.text: Per-FUNCTION reference multisets. The granularity a defect actually has. ... A seeded defect edits ONE function; so the comparison has to be one function wide or the signal drowns in the rest of the patch.
claims.why: Function body is incomplete (truncated at end of chunk); cannot verify that it returns per-function multisets.

claims.text: Aggregating a delta per commit was wrong and the measurement showed it: this repository's history is nearly all growth (median +354 references per commit, median -0), so any 'removed vs added' rule is trivially never true at commit scale, and a guard deleted beside a new 300-line module is invisible.
claims.why: Claim references empirical measurement not present in this chunk; no code or data to verify.

observations.what: _refs_by_function is incomplete; function body truncated at end of chunk.
measure_commit uses git show with caret syntax (sha^:path); may fail on root commit (no parent) or on non-commit objects.
_int_arg uses silent fallback; no logging or warning emitted on malformed input.
commit_shas returns list of SHAs; no deduplication or sorting guarantee beyond git log order.
specificity returns dict with rows containing per_file data; could be large for 80 commits.
The comment block before _git describes the specificity arm rationale but is not a docstring; no code enforces the hypothesis.
